lesson.title: Review Day: Publishing Our Opinion Paragraph
lesson.subject: ela

contentBlocks.text: This week you learned opinions, reasons, organization, and linking words. Today is review day — let's polish everything into one finished, published opinion paragraph.

Read back through your paragraph from this week. Check: is your opinion clear? Do you have at least two real reasons? Does your closing sentence wrap it up? Have you used at least one linking word? Revise anything that needs it, then write your final, polished version.
You just wrote and published a complete, real opinion paragraph — a genuine piece of persuasive writing! Next week, we'll keep building your reading and writing skills.

objectives: Revise and finalize a complete opinion paragraph, checking for opinion clarity, reasons, organization, and linking words
Self-identify which part of opinion writing feels most secure and which needs more practice
materialsNeeded: This week's four worksheets/drafts, for revision
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Read back through the whole week's opinion paragraph draft together.
2. Use the checklist (clear opinion, reasons, closing, linking words) to identify what needs revision.
3. Revise together, then write the final polished version.
4. Praise effort and progress across the whole week, not just today's final product.
5. Close by reading the finished, published paragraph aloud with pride.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus revision on just one or two checklist items rather than trying to perfect everything at once
Ready for more: add a third reason or a stronger closing sentence to the final version
For a child who enjoys sharing their work, have them read the finished paragraph to a family member
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a revision and publishing activity — there is no single right/wrong answer. Check that the final paragraph includes a clear opinion, at least two reasons, a closing sentence, and at least one linking word.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: A dedicated review/publishing day after a full week of opinion-writing components matches the platform's established pacing pattern, and models the real writing-process step of revising toward a finished piece.
